summaryMarkdown:
## Proposed launch
Move Cedar Vale's Oracle E-Business Suite 12.2 production estate and supporting integrations from its Ohio data center to OCI. The customer and North Bridge Systems own implementation. Launch Engine will review architecture decisions, coordinate Oracle service specialists, and track open platform blockers.

The initial migration wave covers nonproduction validation before a customer-led production cutover.

workloads.name: EBS production application and database
workloads.descriptionMarkdown: Production EBS application tier and Oracle Database. The partner proposes a parallel OCI build followed by a customer-approved cutover. **Final sizing and support validation remain open.**
workloads.otherOciServicesMarkdown: OCI Load Balancer, Vault, and DNS

techStack.compute: Customer-managed x86 servers in the Ohio data center. Confirm the final CPU and memory inventory before sizing OCI.
techStack.vmsContainers: 14 Linux VMs run the EBS application tier and supporting jobs. No containers are in scope.
techStack.storage: 22 TB of database storage plus NFS application attachments. Validate IOPS, throughput, mount dependencies, and the transfer window.
techStack.database: Oracle Database 19c supports EBS 12.2. Confirm EBS certification, database options, licensing, and the migration sequence.
techStack.integration: Order, procurement, and manufacturing interfaces use batch jobs and file transfers. Preserve connectivity to the retained manufacturing execution system.
techStack.networking: Ohio data center hub uses MPLS, corporate DNS, and firewall policy sets. The customer network team owns routing and firewall changes; FastConnect delivery is still pending.
techStack.security: Corporate identity provider, centralized SIEM, and privileged-access controls are in use. Review role mappings, secrets, and audit retention.
techStack.highAvailability: Multiple application nodes serve production. Confirm database failover design and application session behavior before final sizing.
techStack.disasterRecovery: Nightly RMAN backups and a manual secondary-site recovery runbook exist. Validate restore procedures against the four-hour RTO target.
techStack.other: Freeze EBS changes during cutover. The customer owns rollback approval, and the partner owns the detailed migration runbook.

0.note: Custom EBS extensions need dependency testing.

5.note: Identity federation and privileged access require review.

6.note: Cutover must protect open orders and support rollback.

blockers.name: Database target design validation
blockers.descriptionMarkdown: Confirm the proposed Oracle Database target, EBS support position, and license assumptions before finalizing the production architecture.
blockers.nextStepMarkdown: Pursuits architect will review the design with the database specialist and customer licensing contact.

blockers.name: Ashburn compute capacity review
blockers.descriptionMarkdown: The current estimate calls for a peak of 96 OCPUs during parallel validation. Region capacity is not yet reserved.
blockers.nextStepMarkdown: Confirm shape mix and need-by dates, then submit a capacity review request.

workloads.name: EBS nonproduction validation environments
workloads.descriptionMarkdown: Build a representative OCI nonproduction environment for performance, functional, and operational testing before production migration.
workloads.applicationUseOther: Preproduction validation and user acceptance testing
workloads.otherOciServicesMarkdown: OCI Vault for test credentials and Object Storage for masked backup files.

techStack.compute: Shared customer-managed x86 hosts support development, test, and UAT. Capture peak test-cycle demand.
techStack.vmsContainers: Linux VMs host EBS 12.2 clones and scheduled jobs. Preserve representative application topology for UAT.
techStack.storage: Masked database clones and application files use shared storage. Confirm clone refresh size and backup retention.
techStack.database: Oracle Database 19c nonproduction clones require masking before transfer. Validate character sets, patches, and refresh procedures.
techStack.integration: Test endpoints connect to finance and supply-chain simulators. The partner owns endpoint mapping and batch sequencing.
techStack.networking: Nonproduction uses isolated data center subnets. Confirm private access, DNS resolution, and test firewall rules.
techStack.security: Customer security policy requires masked data and separate nonproduction credentials. Validate role mappings before UAT.
techStack.highAvailability: Test environments use single application nodes. Match production behavior where required for acceptance tests.
techStack.disasterRecovery: Nonproduction environments restore from backup rather than using a dedicated DR site. Test a full restore before UAT.
techStack.other: Use representative month-end transactions and custom concurrent programs. The customer application owner approves the UAT evidence.

0.note: Custom extensions and concurrent programs require representative tests.

5.note: Mask personal and commercially sensitive data before copying test databases.

successMeasures.shortDescription: EBS completes a representative month-end cycle with no unresolved critical defects.

successMeasures.shortDescription: Business owners validate order creation, receiving, and finance posting after cutover.
